batch_strategy: Measure local composition responses where previous corrective labels failed to transfer, test endpoint-specific loading effects, and add structural comparisons with a clear role in distinguishing retention representations. Include a matched aromatic-ether response experiment and targeted follow-up of the cinnamic-acid completion tail. Packet predictions remain frozen; historical acquisition errors and single-predictor quantile widths are treated as supporting signals, not current residuals or calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: Cinnamic acid at 1/1 with 1500 uL DCM loading solvent; packet V1/V2 prediction 6.353295803070068/101.22096252441406 mL. Observed f90a5a5a54509c085ebd at 2000 uL gave 6.51/108.89 mL. This nearly mass-matched loading-solvent-volume contrast tests whether the long completion tail transfers across recorded loading conditions; the small density difference remains an input.

Cinnamic acid at 2/1; packet prediction 12.265414237976074/71.45360565185547 mL. Loading conditions exactly match the selected 1500 uL 1/1 and 5/1 experiments. This measures the currently unknown intermediate response after f90a5a5a54509c085ebd revealed a very large historical V2 underestimate without a comparable onset error.

Cinnamic acid at 5/1 and 1500 uL DCM; packet prediction 14.633707046508789/51.294864654541016 mL. Completes the selected three-composition series at identical loading. Together with measured 6802f0b28c5a0c7b4c2a and f90a5a5a54509c085ebd, it distinguishes a persistent broad interval from a response concentrated around particular compositions.

Naphthylethanol at 2/1, loading-matched to 48853fd78c77153b963a at 5/1; packet prediction 16.709505081176758/23.731473922729492 mL. The measured anchor was 51.43/98.38 mL and had a 62.95 mL historical completion underestimate. This tests the very large predicted contraction after the first corrective label.

Naphthylmethanol at 2/1, loading-matched to 614873124b33029a924c; packet prediction 12.281478881835938/19.56791877746582 mL. Its measured 5/1 endpoints were 26.06/57.81 mL. The common-composition comparison with selected naphthylethanol tests transfer of donor environment and scaffold differences, retaining their different loading-solvent volumes.

Para-methylbenzyl alcohol at 2/1; packet prediction 11.609933853149414/17.028106689453125 mL. Conditions match 716d04ed1943f0708912 at 5/1, measured 20.92/34.02 mL. This constrains the response of a benzyl alcohol whose first prediction substantially underestimated both endpoints and complements the measured methoxybenzyl alcohol e4fd83fb3852eb354a66.

The remote aryl tertiary alcohol m51 at 10/1 and 50 uL sample volume; packet prediction 46.672603607177734/81.04517364501953 mL. Loading matches observed 2/1 row a1ea7a9303a5fc7a7b0f, measured 10.77/15.87 mL. Tests whether the large predicted weak-eluent response is appropriate for this tertiary donor environment rather than transferred too broadly from primary alcohol corrections.

The remote aryl secondary alcohol m60 at 10/1; packet prediction 42.93207550048828/73.7696762084961 mL. Loading matches measured 1/1 row c5594361764ec76761e2, which gave 5.02/14.92 mL. This tests weak-eluent extrapolation for a secondary alcohol and helps distinguish donor accessibility from a generic alcohol retention correction.

3-Phenylpropanol at 10/1; packet prediction 44.90947341918945/76.53330993652344 mL. The same loading has measured anchors 53c1be5b96937954b9fa at 2/1 and c46b86dae7e6845f08cd at 1/1. This supplies a primary-alcohol response reference for the selected secondary and tertiary alcohol tests, with loading differences retained across molecules.

Ortho-methoxyacetophenone at 50/1 and intermediate 100 uL sample volume; packet prediction 8.030936241149902/27.92269515991211 mL. Observed 52b9af4df1f1e7cd4d9b and c82167c626a1495ef750 at 50 and 150 uL had onsets 11.65 and 1.01 mL but almost identical completion volumes. This tests interpolation of a loading effect the predictor still scarcely represents.

Para-methoxybenzaldehyde at 10/1 and 150 uL sample volume; packet prediction 10.823808670043945/36.8455696105957 mL. Measured 100 uL row 319e89d7000731f64e7f gave 4.78/36.82 mL. This loading contrast tests whether its unusually early onset is associated with loading, as seen for m127, or remains an isolated observation.

Para-methoxybenzaldehyde at 2/1 and 100 uL; packet prediction 4.982568264007568/16.432783126831055 mL. Loading exactly matches measured 10/1 row 319e89d7000731f64e7f. Combined with the selected 10/1 loading contrast, this separates composition response from loading-associated onset behavior and constrains V1 and V2 independently.

Methoxy-substituted salicylaldehyde at 5/1 and 150 uL; packet prediction 14.093523025512695/15.812729835510254 mL. Measured a7bc3fb68bdecbbe086f at 10/1 had reversed endpoints, whereas 5079d0dfcde65893b224 at 2/1 gave 4.88/15.80 mL. Tests the predicted narrow intermediate interval; both existing anchors used 100 uL, so loading remains a covariate.

The same salicylaldehyde in pure EA at 150 uL; packet prediction 9.24853515625/17.933940887451172 mL. Loading exactly matches the selected 5/1 experiment, whose predicted completion is earlier despite weaker eluent. This tests an endpoint-specific predicted inversion while 8e99350aac88fae9186b and 88cccd3e55677c52f9b7 caution against propagating a late, near-zero-width family response.

Tert-butyl acetoacetate at 10/1 and 100 uL; packet prediction 22.422677993774414/44.52422332763672 mL. Measured 50/1 row 3fc05dc2025715e68174 at this loading gave 42.22/88.03 mL, while stronger-eluent observations are early. This locates the composition transition for a common beta-ketoester arrangement without assuming the response of the multifunctional esters transfers unchanged.

Ethyl benzoylacetate at 50/1 and 100 uL; packet prediction 12.359506607055664/26.860416412353516 mL. Observations ce11189a0e59d1798306 at 10/1 and 5879dc8ccb560446d54c at 5/1 have much shorter completion volumes than several other beta-ketoesters. This tests whether the comparatively low weak-eluent scale persists; their differing sample loads remain covariates.

Cyclopropyl beta-ketoester at 10/1 and 100 uL; packet prediction 23.520217895507812/42.262306213378906 mL. It matches loading of 2/1 observation 7bd353fc307c5af1997e and fills the composition gap between 20d4b1612cbdd88b6755 and ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f. Those 5/1 and 20/1 anchors used 50 uL, so the new label informs joint loading-strength transfer rather than an isolated slope alone.

Diethyl bromomalonate at 10/1 and 100 uL; packet prediction 6.915778160095215/8.273094177246094 mL. Loading-matched observations b98a7974de322ed42ec0 at 20/1 and 027bbff1ac308c5dd7a1 at 50/1 gave 13.37/24.60 and 26.16/41.80 mL. Tests the predicted abrupt transition to a very short interval, extending the measured distinction between early malonate and more retained substituted carbonyl compounds.

Methylquinoline at 5/1 and 50 uL; packet prediction 44.27485275268555/86.32075500488281 mL. Loading matches 1/1 reference b6229f0445560a4a54ed. Recent 10/1 observation 9e3ce3497298084abd83 was 59.58/106.50 mL with substantial historical underprediction, but used 100 uL. This tests the corrected intermediate retention scale while retaining the loading difference.

Ethyl nicotinate at 5/1; packet prediction 28.49994659423828/71.10884857177734 mL. Loading matches both measured c76d0420b34df595c0c9 at 10/1 and 22f82413c75481d74e9b at 2/1. The latter exposed a 33.80 mL historical V2 overestimate. This discriminates intermediate curve shapes after that correction, contrasting with methylquinoline's remaining weak-eluent underprediction.

2,6-Dimethoxybenzaldehyde at 1/1 and 100 uL in 300 uL DCM; packet prediction 11.513692855834961/27.078332901000977 mL. Loading exactly matches 5/1 observation 74cf50c6ec476a394b01, measured 42.96/73.10 mL. The label tests a large predicted strong-eluent transition; measured 2/1 reference facbcedbecb46072b04c also remains late but has a different loading setup.

1,3,5-Trimethoxybenzene at 2/1 and 150 uL; packet prediction 12.733643531799316/30.13779640197754 mL. Together with the selected 5/1 point, directly tests the model's predicted reversal of the usual solvent-strength trend at identical loading. Existing 8d48112406e3064efdbc and aaf45151a9b4a7a5fa5c do not establish this intermediate response.

1,3,5-Trimethoxybenzene at 5/1 and 150 uL; packet prediction 6.563883304595947/10.721467018127441 mL. Completes the matched pair whose 2/1 prediction is substantially later at both endpoints. Pure-EA observation aaf45151a9b4a7a5fa5c supplies a loading-matched strong-eluent anchor. Measurement can distinguish genuine recorded nonmonotonicity from an interpolation failure.

First dimethoxy-methylbenzene label at 2/1 and 150 uL; packet prediction 7.187114715576172/16.643089294433594 mL. Its molecule is absent from the observed set, with maximum similarity 0.407. Paired with its selected 5/1 point and the trimethoxybenzene pair, this tests whether a shared predicted response inversion transfers across related ether substitution patterns.

The same unseen dimethoxy-methylbenzene at 5/1 and identical loading; packet prediction 3.573129177093506/8.874519348144531 mL. The two-molecule, two-composition experiment tests both response direction and structural transfer. A single label would not distinguish an incorrect molecular retention scale from an incorrect composition dependence.

First biphenylcarboxaldehyde label at 10/1; packet prediction 11.257716178894043/25.60447883605957 mL. It provides an aromatic-carbonyl comparison with the selected biphenyl butanone and measured fused-aromatic ketone b0cc544ceb575bae4069. The aim is to test carbonyl context and aromatic topology; different density and loading-solvent volumes remain model inputs.

First biphenyl butanone label at 10/1; packet prediction 5.8001227378845215/16.21088981628418 mL. Its prediction is appreciably earlier than the selected biphenyl aldehyde despite sharing the extended aromatic framework. Observed 92f7fe9d8581717a9949 and 4c46ceefd6147b1e0a7a show that aldehyde/ketone context can accompany large retention differences, motivating a structural-transfer test without assuming their direction here.

First bromonaphthaldehyde label at 10/1; packet prediction 14.200745582580566/31.24342918395996 mL, observed-set similarity 0.4375. It tests transfer to a fused, halogenated aromatic carbonyl using measured naphthaldehyde reference 783cf2454912fc14bb80 and acetylnaphthalene b0cc544ceb575bae4069 as related, differently conditioned evidence. This expands a structural relationship rather than selecting novelty alone.

Cyanoacetophenone at 5/1 and 50 uL; packet prediction 12.31517219543457/28.148391723632812 mL. Loading matches measured 10/1 row b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11, which gave 31.50/67.28 mL. This tests a large predicted response and contrasts with the much earlier 10/1 cyano-benzophenone observation c6e78c97267cbb98dc22, constraining acceptor context rather than a universal nitrile correction.

Para-nitroacetophenone at 10/1 and 100 uL; packet prediction 32.67294692993164/70.41220092773438 mL. Loading matches 5/1 observation 9de8f9fed06ef9d5befa, measured 13.74/30.63 mL. That acquisition overpredicted completion, so this weaker-eluent point tests whether retraining repaired the response shape or only the measured scale.

Para-nitrobenzaldehyde at 10/1 and 50 uL; packet prediction 26.854894638061523/62.99934768676758 mL. Loading matches measured 5/1 reference 3e69cf586f3eb0f0fa8c, which gave 11.11/26.89 mL. Alongside nitroacetophenone, it tests transfer of a steep nitro-carbonyl response, while their different sample loads prevent treating the cross-molecule contrast as fully controlled.

Acetoxybenzaldehyde at 5/1; packet prediction 16.640098571777344/40.161949157714844 mL. Loading matches measured 2/1 row 5522a1ec1f8e39cedb13 and 10/1 row 351c17dfa8f46a8cb40a, which span 6.27/25.12 to 39.13/81.40 mL. This locates the transition between verified endpoints and tests whether onset and completion require different curve shapes.

hypotheses.content: Aromatic carbonyl composition responses depend strongly on neighboring functional groups and structural context. Correcting one retention anchor does not reliably establish the slope or transfer the correction to another aldehyde or ketone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The pool contains many aromatic carbonyl rows. Intermediate composition labels and connected structural comparisons can teach transferable interactions while preventing a broad polarity correction from degrading already accurate families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the cyano and nitro carbonyls show their predicted steep responses, where is the acetoxybenzaldehyde transition, and do the new biphenyl carbonyl labels support structural transfer?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing compounds need scaffold-specific composition responses. Recent stronger-eluent labels were accurate for quinoline and aminoacetophenone, overpredicted for ethyl nicotinate, and did not eliminate weak-eluent underprediction for methylquinoline.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate labels distinguish curve shape from a global nitrogen retention offset. The records do not establish protonation states or a single adsorption mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1, does ethyl nicotinate follow the predicted intermediate completion scale, and does methylquinoline retain its corrected long-retention response?

hypotheses.content: The large 5/1 retention scales of several primary arylalkyl alcohols are measured, but their stronger-eluent curves and transfer to secondary or tertiary alcohol environments remain unresolved. Donor environment and distance from the aromatic ring may matter beyond HBD/HBA counts.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected responses connect observed alcohol failures to common donor environments and test whether new corrections generalize appropriately. Structural, loading and loading-solvent differences remain covariates.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the naphthyl and methylbenzyl alcohol intervals contract as predicted at 2/1, and are the predicted long 10/1 intervals supported for remote primary, secondary and tertiary aryl alcohols?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl arrangement produces distinct retention and composition-response scales. Early diethyl malonate does not represent all substituted malonates or beta-ketoesters. Recent multifunctional ester labels also show that a first long-retention anchor can cause excessive extrapolation into stronger eluent.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The beta-carbonyl and ester families occupy many candidate conditions. Labels across different arrangements can teach endpoint-specific solvent responses without assigning an unverified enolization or adsorption mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where are the response transitions for tert-butyl and cyclopropyl beta-ketoesters, does benzoylacetate remain comparatively early at 50/1, and is bromomalonate's predicted short 10/1 interval supported?

hypotheses.content: The predictor gives inverted 2/1-to-5/1 responses for trimethoxybenzene and unseen dimethoxy-methylbenzene, and a sharp strong-eluent transition for 2,6-dimethoxybenzaldehyde. These are untested model behaviors, not established chemical response curves.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A matched two-molecule, two-composition experiment can distinguish a common interpolation failure from scaffold-specific responses. The aldehyde label tests whether a neighboring carbonyl changes the transition. These relationships may generalize across aromatic ether rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At identical loading, are the two ether compounds actually later at 2/1 than at 5/1, and does the dimethoxybenzaldehyde interval contract sharply at 1/1?

hypotheses.content: Cinnamic acid has a reproducibly long measured completion scale across the two supplied compositions, while onset remains early. Its detailed composition dependence and sensitivity to loading-solvent volume remain unknown.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The 91.10 mL historical V2 underestimate identifies an endpoint-specific failure that a generic shift in both endpoints would not repair. A controlled response series can constrain how this corrective label spreads across the acid's rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the long 1/1 completion persist with 1500 uL loading solvent, and how do onset and completion change from 1/1 through 2/1 to 5/1 at that fixed loading setup?

hypotheses.content: Loading-associated onset changes can be large while completion changes little, whereas current predictions are nearly sample-volume invariant. The ortho-methoxy ketone supports this association at two compositions; transfer to the early-onset para-methoxy aldehyde is an untested hypothesis.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The density-times-volume feature varies throughout the Row-distribution. These experiments test endpoint-specific loading dependence and its interaction with composition; run variation or missing information may still contribute.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the ortho ketone's intermediate loading interpolate its 50/1 onset shift, and does changing the para-methoxy aldehyde's load alter onset without substantially changing completion?

hypotheses.content: The previous idea of a repeatable late, near-zero-width salicylaldehyde-family response is weakened. The unusual original records remain measured evidence, but subsequent loading and positional-isomer labels gave early onsets and ordinary positive intervals. Loading effects, run variation and missing experimental information remain unresolved explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: An unusual label can propagate an incorrect response across related molecules and conditions. Targeted follow-up can constrain that propagation without discarding or silently altering the original observations.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: For methoxy-substituted salicylaldehyde, does a matched 150 uL 5/1-to-pure-EA comparison support the predicted narrow intermediate interval or completion-volume inversion?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes reinforce context-specific failure repair and weaken several broader explanations. Sulfoxide measured 27.42/52.38 mL at 5/1 and 12.32/22.67 mL at 2/1: the first weak-eluent correction had overshot the intermediate response. The multifunctional beta-ketoester's measured 10/1, 5/1 and 2/1 sequence was 44.09/91.85, 20.22/43.11 and 9.23/17.90 mL, rejecting its previously predicted V2 inversion. Methoxyethyl acetoacetate likewise contracted more than predicted, while the cyclopropyl beta-ketoester remained underestimated at 20/1. I therefore emphasize response transitions across carbonyl arrangements rather than another global retention increase. The naphthyl alcohols and methylbenzyl alcohol exposed substantial structural-transfer failures, so their stronger-eluent responses and transfer to other donor environments deserve measurement. Nitrogen outcomes stayed heterogeneous: quinoline and aminoacetophenone stronger-eluent predictions were close, ethyl nicotinate was overpredicted, and methylquinoline remained substantially underestimated at 10/1. The ortho-methoxy ketone's intermediate 20/1 onset and very early high-loading 50/1 onset strengthen the loading-associated endpoint question. Bromosalicylaldehyde at another loading and its positional isomer did not reproduce the late, almost zero-width pure-EA behavior; the methoxy analogue also gave an ordinary interval at 2/1. This weakens family-wide propagation of those anomalies. Cinnamic acid instead revealed a much longer 1/1 completion volume, 108.89 mL, with onset still near 6.51 mL, making its endpoint-specific response a separate question. The bulky aldehyde, acetylnaphthalene and substituted tetralone predictions were comparatively close, reducing the case for allocating many labels to novelty or lipophilicity alone. All cited acquisition errors are historical, not residuals of the current predictor.
batch_rationale: The batch combines local experiments that answer distinct generalization questions. Six alcohol labels test both repair of newly observed failures and transfer across donor environments. The cinnamic-acid series controls composition and provides a loading-solvent-volume comparison to the existing 1/1 record. The ortho-methoxy ketone and para-methoxy aldehyde experiments address an input dependence that the current predictions scarcely express, while the salicylaldehyde pair tests propagation of unusual endpoint records. Four carbonyl/ester labels and two nitrogen labels locate response transitions after earlier corrective labels sometimes transferred poorly. The aromatic-ether experiment uses a matched two-by-two design because one label per molecule would not distinguish a wrong retention scale from a wrong response direction. New biphenyl carbonyls and bromonaphthaldehyde extend structural coverage through specific comparisons to measured aromatic carbonyl families. Other aromatic carbonyl follow-ups connect nitrile, nitro and acetoxy environments to measured anchors. Repeated identical experiment tuples were avoided. Large predicted volumes are selected only where they discriminate response hypotheses; interval width is treated as a chromatographic outcome, and single-model quantile widths are not interpreted as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The intended benefit is improved joint structure-condition prediction of both endpoints across the Row-distribution, with recorded loading differences preserved and unrecorded experimental factors acknowledged.
